requirements.requirement: node2 is placed on its own VLAN 10 over the shared link (802.1Q sub-interface, addressed on 10.10.10.0/24)
requirements.summary: eth1.10 sub-interface created with 10.10.10.11/24, persisted via ifcfg-eth1.10 and route-eth1.10 files, 8021q module load persisted. Confirmed present with correct address/route both immediately after configuration and after a full reboot (new boot_id e54376a6...).

requirements.requirement: node3 is placed on its own VLAN 20 over the shared link (802.1Q sub-interface, addressed on 10.10.20.0/24)
requirements.summary: eth1.20 sub-interface created with 10.10.20.12/24, persisted via ifcfg-eth1.20 and route-eth1.20 files. Confirmed present with correct address/route both immediately after configuration and after a full reboot (new boot_id 1627b8d1...).

requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) routes between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 (IP forwarding enabled, no blocking firewall, both vif addresses present, config committed/saved)
requirements.summary: eth1 vif 10 (10.10.10.254/24) and vif 20 (10.10.20.254/24) set, committed, and saved to config.boot; ip_forward=1 confirmed; no firewall configured to block traffic. Interfaces confirmed present both before and after a full node1 reboot (new boot_id edc2bd6f...).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can still reach each other, routed through node1, without breaking their existing internet/mgmt egress
requirements.summary: Bidirectional ping between node2 (10.10.10.11) and node3 (10.10.20.12) succeeds with ttl=63, confirming a single routed hop through node1. Ping to 8.8.8.8 from both nodes still succeeds via eth0's untouched default route, showing egress preserved. Connectivity also re-verified after each of the three sequential node reboots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with pre/post boot identity, acknowledgement, and recovered state
requirements.summary: All three nodes were sequentially restarted with a captured pre-restart boot_id, a background-scheduled reboot acknowledgement, connection-loss during the reboot window, a new post-restart boot_id, and recovered VLAN interface/route/forwarding state plus restored cross-VLAN connectivity, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots (which show matching before/after boot_id transitions for all three nodes).

overall_summary: The executor successfully segmented node2 onto VLAN 10 and node3 onto VLAN 20 as 802.1Q sub-interfaces over the shared eth1 link, configured node1 (VyOS) to route between the two VLANs with IP forwarding enabled and no blocking firewall, and directly verified bidirectional cross-VLAN reachability (ttl=63 confirming the routed hop) while preserving each node's independent internet egress via eth0. All configuration was made persistent (VyOS config.boot save; RHEL ifcfg/route files) and this persistence, plus full functional recovery, was directly demonstrated across sequential reboots of all three nodes with matching boot-identity transitions cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Package-health checks for node2 and node3 timed out in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so package-manager consistency on the RHEL nodes could not be independently verified.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor timeline rather than an independent prepare snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: One transient, self-corrected misconfiguration occurred: the first ifcfg-eth1.10/eth1.20 attempts on node2/node3 (cmd-f5055db0f8774b62, cmd-9f2d885e675443fd) included a GATEWAY= line that installed a competing zero-metric default route via the VLAN sub-interface, which would have hijacked internet-bound traffic away from eth0. This was recognized and immediately corrected in the very next commands (cmd-641db4f69e6e465d, cmd-6d584624e4644ca4), which rewrote the ifcfg files without GATEWAY and added scoped route-eth1.NN files instead; the final verified route tables show only the intended single default route via eth0 plus the specific peer-VLAN route, so no residue remained. Two earlier unprivileged attempts to write ifcfg files (cmd-8866bbb1337f40cc, cmd-2e614d40178440ec) failed with permission denied and made no state changes. The lifecycle diff for node1 confirms package-health (dpkg), no new failed services, and no unexplained residue beyond expected reboot artifacts (new systemd-private tmp dirs, reboot.log) on all three nodes.
